answer: A writing licence is granted only for a manuscript the applicant copies by hand with a quill, leaves sealed beneath a crystal wafer, and lodges at a district scriptorium that records the hand-stroke rhythm and the ink drawn down. Every deposited manuscript must then be read and countersigned by two other claimants in the same cohort, so a cohort of k copies demands about k squared proofreading shifts. A farm running many clones crowds its own reading desk and pays twice over for every copy it must read and be read; the quiet applicant sees a clear horizon.
